name: 3D point cloud learning

conventions.text: Bracket a segmentation network with real point-cloud renders: the scanned scene at the input end and a scene coloured by predicted class at the output end.
Label every stage with its (points, channels) shape, e.g. (N, 32), (N/4, 64) or n x 64, so point count and feature width can be read along the row.
Write the point operations (sampling, kNN grouping, pooling, MLP) as short text on the arrows between data boxes, not as boxes of their own.
Draw each tensor as its own box with its shape written inside, rotated 90 degrees.
Run the encoder-decoder straight along one row (no U fold) and route the skips as nested orthogonal arcs over the top of the row, the outermost joining the first and last stages.
When classification and segmentation are both shown, draw them as two stacked rows aligned on the same left-hand columns, so the shared early stages line up.
Use square-cornered flat rectangles with thin outlines rather than rounded boxes.

source: summarised from the evidence cards listed under each convention
